literal: In the Taishi era of Jin, the relevant offices memorialized: "In the feudal states, for those from kings and dukes downward who come to court, each of the four quarters shall be divided into two turns; in three years the cycle is complete, and when the cycle is complete it begins anew.
idiomatic: During Jin's Taishi reign, officials submitted a memorial: princes and lesser lords coming to court from the four quarters should each take two turns, completing the full round in three years; when the round was finished, the count would start again.

literal: If there is an emergency at the appointed time, one may defer to the following year.
idiomatic: If an unforeseen circumstance arose at the appointed time, the visit could be postponed to the following year.

literal: After coming to court, one must wait a full three years before returning; one may not count from the original reckoning.
idiomatic: After a court visit, another full three years had to pass before one might come again; the original schedule could not be resumed.

literal: The court ceremony of holding a bi shall follow the old system of court visits.
idiomatic: The court audience rite, with the presentation of a bi jade, was to follow the former court-visit regulations.

literal: In years when one does not come to court, each state shall send a minister to present gifts of courtesy.
idiomatic: In years when a lord did not attend in person, each state was to send a minister bearing a courtesy mission.

literal: " The memorial was approved.
idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

literal: East of the Yangtze, princes and marquises did not go to their fiefs; those granted appointments abroad were treated like regional governors and prefects of two thousand shi rank, and there was likewise no system of court visits and courtesy missions; thus this ritual was abandoned.
idiomatic: In the south, princes and marquises no longer took up their fiefs; those posted abroad were treated like regional inspectors and two-thousand-shi prefects, and the court-visit and courtesy-mission system likewise lapsed—so the rite fell out of use.

literal: At the New Year's Day grand assembly, a White Tiger goblet was set up in the hall courtyard.
idiomatic: At the New Year's grand assembly, a White Tiger goblet was placed in the palace courtyard.

literal: A white tiger was placed atop the goblet lid; if someone was able to offer blunt counsel, this goblet would be opened and wine drunk from it.
idiomatic: A white tiger was mounted on the lid; if someone wished to speak blunt truth, this goblet was opened and wine drunk from it.

literal: According to the Book of Rites: when Zhi Daozi died and had not yet been buried, Duke Ping was drinking wine, with Shi Kuang and Li Diao in attendance, and bells were being struck.
idiomatic: The Book of Rites records that when Zhi Daozi died and had not yet been buried, Duke Ping was drinking wine while Shi Kuang and Li Diao attended and bells were struck.

literal: Du Kui came from outside, heard the bell sounds, and said: "Where is he?
idiomatic: Du Kui came in from outside, heard the bells, and asked, "Where is he?"

literal: " They replied: "In the inner chamber.
idiomatic: They answered, "In the inner chamber."

literal: " Du Kui entered the inner chamber, ascended the steps, poured wine, and said: "Kuang, drink this.
idiomatic: Du Kui entered the chamber, climbed the steps, poured wine, and said, "Kuang, drink this."

literal: " He poured again and said: "Diao, drink this.
idiomatic: He poured again and said, "Diao, drink this."

literal: " He poured once more, sat facing north in the hall and drank it himself, then descended and hurried out.
idiomatic: He poured once more, sat facing north in the hall and drank, then went down the steps and hurried out.

literal: Duke Ping called him back and said: "Kui, earlier your heart may have been open toward me, and for that reason I did not speak with you.
idiomatic: Duke Ping called him back and said, "Kui, earlier I thought your heart was open to me, and so I did not speak with you."

literal: Why did you make Kuang drink?
idiomatic: "Why did you make Kuang drink?"

literal: " He replied: "On the days of zi and mao one does not make music; with Zhi Daozi's body in the hall, how much greater was this than a day of zi or mao!
idiomatic: He replied, "On the days of zi and mao one does not make music; with Zhi Daozi's body still in the hall, this was a day of zi and mao in the fullest sense."

literal: Kuang is the Grand Music Master.
idiomatic: Kuang is the Grand Music Master.

literal: He was not admonished, and for that reason I made him drink.
idiomatic: He was not admonished, and for that I made him drink.

literal: " "Why did you make Diao drink?
idiomatic: "Why did you make Diao drink?"

literal: " He replied: "Diao is the lord's intimate attendant.
idiomatic: He replied, "Diao is your intimate attendant.

literal: For a single drink and a single meal he forgot the lord's grief, and for that reason I made him drink.
idiomatic: For one cup and one meal he forgot your grief, and for that I made him drink."

literal: " "Why did you drink?
idiomatic: "And why did you drink?"

literal: " He replied: "I, Kui, am only a cook who supplies knives and spoons; yet I dared to share in knowing how to guard against impropriety, and for that reason I drank.
idiomatic: He replied, "I, Kui, am only a cook who supplies knives and spoons; yet I dared to share in guarding against impropriety, and for that I drank."

literal: " Duke Ping said: "I too have done wrong.
idiomatic: Duke Ping said, "I too have been at fault.

literal: Pour and make me drink.
idiomatic: Pour and make me drink."

literal: " Du Kui washed the cup and raised it aloft.
idiomatic: Du Kui washed the cup and raised it high.

literal: The duke told the attendants: "If I die, you must never discontinue this cup.
idiomatic: The duke told his attendants, "When I die, you must never let this cup fall out of use."

literal: " Down to the present day, after the sacrifice is complete, when the cup is raised aloft, it is called "Du's Toast."
idiomatic: Down to the present, after the offering is complete, raising the cup aloft is called "Du's Toast."

literal: The White Tiger goblet was probably the surviving form of Du's Toast.
idiomatic: The White Tiger goblet was likely a surviving form of Du's Toast.

literal: The painting of a tiger was likely added by later generations, intending that those who speak should be fierce as a tiger, without any fear or restraint.
idiomatic: Painting it as a tiger was probably a later addition, meant to make speakers as fierce as tigers, without fear or restraint.

literal: In Han, Emperor Gaozu fixed the first month of Qin as the year's start in the tenth month; though Emperor Wu later changed to the Xia calendar, at the new moon they still held regular feasts and assemblies like the New Year's rites.
idiomatic: Han began with Gaozu's tenth-month new year, taken from Qin; though Wu later adopted the Xia calendar, the new-moon feast still followed the New Year's rites.

literal: In Wei and Jin, on the winter solstice they received congratulations from all states and the hundred officials, followed by a small assembly.
idiomatic: Under Wei and Jin, the winter solstice brought congratulations from all the realms and the hundred officials, followed by a lesser court gathering.

literal: The ceremony was second in rank to New Year's Day; Jin had annotations on it.
idiomatic: The ceremony ranked below New Year's Day; Jin preserved detailed notes on it.

literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Yongchu of Song, an edict said: "The envoys for celebrating the winter solstice may or may not be sent; labor and service should be economized; henceforth all may cease entirely.
idiomatic: In the eighth month of Song's first Yongchu year, an edict declared: "Winter-solstice envoys need not always be sent; public labor should be reduced, and such missions may now all be suspended.

literal: Only the great celebration of New Year's Day must not be abolished.
idiomatic: Only the great New Year's celebration must not be abandoned.

literal: County and district envoys sent for the winter solstice to prefectures and regional command headquarters should likewise be stopped."
idiomatic: Winter-solstice envoys sent from counties and districts to prefectures and regional command posts should likewise be stopped."

literal: Sun Quan at first made his capital at Wuchang and Jiankang, and did not establish suburban altars.
idiomatic: When Sun Quan first ruled from Wuchang and Jiankang, he did not establish suburban altars.

literal: At the end of his reign, in the eleventh month of the first year of Taixi, he sacrificed at the southern suburb; the site is now at Jiao Zhong, more than ten li south of Moling County.
idiomatic: Near the end of his reign, in the eleventh month of Taixi 1, he sacrificed at the southern suburb; the site lies at Jiao Zhong, more than ten li south of present-day Moling County.

literal: When the Jin house moved south, they established the southern suburb at the si position, which was not the meaning of the yang position spoken of in ritual.
idiomatic: After the Jin crossed south, they placed the southern suburb in the si direction—not the yang position that ritual prescribed.

literal: In the ninth month of the third year of Daming of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Ai argued: "The position for suburban sacrifice—in remotest antiquity nothing has been heard of it.
idiomatic: In the ninth month of Xiaowu's third Daming year, Xu Ai, Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, argued: "The site of suburban sacrifice is nowhere recorded in deepest antiquity.

literal: The Book of Rites says: "Burning firewood on the great mound is sacrifice to Heaven.
idiomatic: The Book of Rites says, "Burning firewood on the great mound is sacrifice to Heaven.

literal: " "Establishing the altar at the southern suburb is taking the yang position."
idiomatic: Establishing the altar at the southern suburb means taking the yang position."

literal: " In early Han, the suburban rites at Ganquan and Hedong were confused in position; in the end they were also moved to the north and south of Chang'an.
idiomatic: In early Han the Ganquan and Hedong suburban rites shifted sites repeatedly; in the end they were fixed north and south of Chang'an.

literal: Guangwu succeeded to the throne and fixed the two suburban altars north and south of Luoyang.
idiomatic: When Guangwu restored the dynasty, he fixed the two suburban altars north and south of Luoyang.

literal: When the Jin crossed the river, all were in the north.
idiomatic: After the Jin crossed the Yangtze, all the altars lay to the north.

literal: When the matter of suburban altars was debated, opinions were numerous and inconsistent.
idiomatic: Debates over the suburban altars produced many conflicting views.

literal: Moreover the road south was narrow and expansion had not yet been discussed, so they created a mound altar in the southeast at the si position.
idiomatic: The southern road was too narrow and had not yet been widened, so a mound altar was created in the southeast at the si position.

literal: When the Song received the Mandate, they followed it without change.
idiomatic: When Song received the Mandate, it kept the arrangement unchanged.

literal: Moreover "within the dwellings of the people" does not mean outside the city.
idiomatic: Moreover, placing the altar among inhabited ground was not what ritual meant by "outside the city."

literal: Now that the sacred empire is rebuilt, old statutes are wholly renewed, the southern post road is opened, and the yang road is broadened and extended.
idiomatic: Now the sacred realm has been rebuilt, old regulations fully renewed, the southern post road opened, and the yang road cleared and extended.

literal: I propose that the suburban altar should be moved to true south at noon, to fix Heaven's position.
idiomatic: The suburban altar should be moved to true south at the wu position, thereby fixing Heaven's place."

literal: " Academician Ma Xingzhi, Fu Yu, and Assistant Director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies Lu Cheng all agreed with Xu's proposal.
idiomatic: The academicians Ma Xingzhi and Fu Yu, and Lu Cheng, Assistant Director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies, all agreed with Xu Ai.

literal: Then the suburban altar was moved to the west of Mount Niutou in Moling, directly at the wu position of the palace.
idiomatic: The suburban altar was then moved west of Mount Niutou in Moling, directly on the palace's southern wu axis.

literal: When Emperor Shizu died and the deposed Emperor took the throne, he regarded the old suburban site as auspicious and moved it back to the original place.
idiomatic: After Emperor Shizu died and the Deposed Emperor succeeded, he took the old suburban site to be auspicious and moved the altar back.

literal: The northern suburb was first established in the era of Emperor Chengdi of Jin, originally south of Mount Fuzhou.
idiomatic: The northern suburb was first established under Jin's Emperor Cheng, originally south of Mount Fuzhou.

literal: Emperor Taizu of Song made the site into the Leyou Garden and moved the altar to the northwest of the mountain.
idiomatic: Song's Emperor Taizu turned the site into the Leyou Garden and moved the northern altar to the northwest of the mountain.

literal: Later, when the site became North Lake, it was moved to the northwest of the lake embankment.
idiomatic: Later, when that ground became North Lake, the altar was moved to the northwest of the lake embankment.

literal: The ground was low and muddy; it was moved again to the east of Baishi Village.
idiomatic: The ground there was low and wet, so it was moved again to the east of Baishi Village.

literal: When that site too became a lake, it was moved to the west of the road on the northern plain of Mount Zhong, facing the southern suburb.
idiomatic: When that site too became a lake, the altar was moved west of the road on the northern plain of Mount Zhong, opposite the southern suburb.

literal: Later, when Baishi East Lake was drained, the northern suburb returned to its old site.
idiomatic: Later, when Baishi East Lake was drained, the northern suburb returned to its former site.

literal: For the southern suburb sacrifice, the emperor observed preliminary abstinence for seven days and strict abstinence for three days.
idiomatic: For the southern suburb rite, the emperor kept preliminary abstinence for seven days and strict abstinence for three.

literal: Officials charged with purification did likewise.
idiomatic: Officials responsible for purification did the same.

literal: On the morning of strict abstinence, he presided from the screened seat in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
idiomatic: On the morning of strict abstinence, he took the screened seat in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

literal: He wore a deep-red gauze robe, a black kerchief cap, and the Tongtian golden Boshan crown.
idiomatic: He wore a crimson gauze robe, a black kerchief cap, and the Tongtian golden Boshan crown.

literal: On the day before the sacrifice, at five watches before sunset, the evening victim ceremony was held.
idiomatic: On the eve of the sacrifice, five watches before sunset, the evening victim rite was performed.

literal: Grandees, the Governor of Jingzhao, and all officials took their places east of the altar; the Grand Invocator's clerk led the victim in.
idiomatic: Grandees, the Governor of Jingzhao, and all officials took their places east of the altar while the Grand Invocator's clerk led the victim in.

literal: Upon reaching the placard, they reported to the Sacrificial Victim Director, who knelt and announced: "I request to inspect the victim.
idiomatic: At the placard they reported to the Sacrificial Victim Director, who knelt and said, "I request to inspect the victim."

literal: " Raising his hand, he said: "Fat.
idiomatic: Raising his hand, he declared, "Fat."

literal: " The Grand Invocator circled the victim and, raising his hand, said: "Full.
idiomatic: The Grand Invocator circled the victim and, raising his hand, said, "Full."

literal: " The Grand Invocator led the victim to the kitchen.
idiomatic: The Grand Invocator then led the victim to the kitchen.

literal: With two pottery dou vessels he ladled hair and blood; one was placed before the seat of the August Heaven Spirit, the other before the seat of the Founding Ancestor.
idiomatic: With two pottery dou vessels he ladled hair and blood, placing one before the seat of August Heaven and the other before the Founding Ancestor's seat.

literal: On the day of the sacrifice, at eight watches before dawn, the Grand Invocator presented the offerings and the gentlemen attendants set them out.
idiomatic: On the day of the sacrifice, eight watches before dawn, the Grand Invocator brought forward the offerings and the attendants arranged them.

literal: For the victim, two dappled chestnut horses were used; for the multitude of spirits, one ox.
idiomatic: The principal victim was two dappled chestnut horses; for the host of spirits, one ox.

literal: Sweet wine used ju chang; matting used white thatch grass.
idiomatic: The sweet wine was ju chang; the matting was white thatch grass.

literal: One vessel of dark water; vessels were gourd pottery; wine was held in earthenware goblets and poured with earthenware ladles.
idiomatic: There was one vessel of dark water; gourd pottery was used for vessels, earthenware goblets held the wine, and earthenware ladles poured it.

literal: The bi disc used pale green jade.
idiomatic: The bi disc was of pale green jade.

literal: Two cattail mats each, with no padded cushions laid.
idiomatic: There were two cattail mats each, with no padded cushions beneath.

literal: In antiquity straw mats were used; in Jin east of the river they used cattail.
idiomatic: In antiquity straw mats were used; in Jin south of the Yangtze they used cattail mats.

literal: When the imperial carriage set out, officials observing abstinence and those filling the streets who had gone ahead with the procession each followed according to acting assignments.
idiomatic: When the imperial procession set out, fasting officials and those already lining the streets each took up their acting assignments and followed.

literal: At one watch after the water hour, the emperor donned the dragon robe and Pingshan crown, mounted the golden-root chariot, and arrived outside the east gate of the altar.
idiomatic: One watch into the water hour, the emperor put on the dragon robe and Pingshan crown, mounted the golden-root chariot, and reached the east gate of the altar.

literal: The academicians and Grand Master of Ceremonies led him in to the black enclosure.
idiomatic: The academicians and the Grand Master of Ceremonies led him to the black enclosure.

literal: The Grand Invocator knelt, held the gourd pottery vessel, and poured wine to libate the ground.
idiomatic: The Grand Invocator knelt, took the gourd pottery vessel, and poured wine to libate the ground.

literal: The emperor bowed twice and rose.
idiomatic: The emperor bowed twice and rose.

literal: All ministers likewise bowed twice and prostrated themselves.
idiomatic: All the ministers bowed twice and prostrated themselves.

literal: The Director of Ritual said: "Rise.
idiomatic: The Director of Ritual called, "Rise."

literal: " The academicians and Grand Master of Ceremonies led the emperor to the southern steps; he removed his shoes, ascended the altar, and went to the urn for hand-washing.
idiomatic: The academicians and Grand Master of Ceremonies led the emperor to the southern steps; he removed his shoes, climbed the altar, and went to the urn to wash his hands.

literal: The Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate washed the goblet and knelt to present it to the emperor.
idiomatic: The Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate washed the goblet and knelt to present it to the emperor.

literal: The cup-bearer presented the goblet, poured ju chang, and presented it to the emperor.
idiomatic: The cup-bearer handed over the goblet, poured ju chang, and presented it to the emperor.

literal: He knelt and placed it before the seat of the August Heaven Spirit, bowed twice, and rose.
idiomatic: The emperor knelt and placed it before the seat of August Heaven, bowed twice, and rose.

literal: Next he went before the Founding Ancestor's seat where he was paired with Heaven, held the goblet, knelt and placed the offering, following the same rite as for August Heaven.
idiomatic: Next he went to the Founding Ancestor's seat paired with Heaven, held the goblet, knelt, and offered it with the same rite as to August Heaven.

literal: Facing south and orienting northward, he bowed once and prostrated himself.
idiomatic: Facing south with his back to the north, he bowed once and prostrated himself.

literal: The Grand Invocator ladled the blessing wine from each, combined them in one goblet, knelt and presented it to the emperor, who bowed twice and prostrated himself.
idiomatic: The Grand Invocator ladled the blessing wine from each offering, combined it in one goblet, knelt, and presented it; the emperor bowed twice and prostrated himself.

literal: When he had finished drinking the blessing wine, the academicians and Grand Master of Ceremonies led the emperor down the eastern steps and back to the southern steps.
idiomatic: After drinking the blessing wine, the academicians and Grand Master of Ceremonies led the emperor down the eastern steps and back to the southern steps.

literal: The usher led the Grand Master of Ceremonies up the altar for the secondary offering.
idiomatic: The usher led the Grand Master of Ceremonies up the altar for the secondary offering.

literal: The usher again led the Director of the Imperial Household up the altar for the final offering.
idiomatic: The usher then led the Director of the Imperial Household up the altar for the final offering.

literal: It was finished.
idiomatic: The rite was complete.

literal: Each descended the steps and returned to his original position.
idiomatic: Each descended the steps and returned to his place.

literal: The Grand Invocator dismissed the spirits, knelt, held the gourd pottery vessel, and poured wine to libate the ground.
idiomatic: The Grand Invocator sent off the spirits, knelt, took the gourd pottery vessel, and poured wine to libate the ground.
